question: In the Gupta period, the term Udranga referred to ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**land tax**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Gupta Empire**, which ruled over a significant part of the Indian subcontinent (approximately from **320 CE to 550 CE**), had a well-organized taxation system to support their administration and military.
 
• The revenue collected through **Udranga (land tax)** was utilized for purposes like maintaining administrative functions, supporting the military, and building infrastructure like temples and public facilities.
 
• The Gupta rulers implemented a systematic taxation regime, which included various taxes like **Bali** (tribute), **Bhaga** (share of agricultural produce), and **Kara** (customs duties).
 
• These taxes enabled the government to maintain stability, manage the empire efficiently, and undertake developmental activities.

 
• **Role of Land Tax:**

 
 
• The taxes were used for building **temples**, maintaining public infrastructure, and supporting religious and cultural activities.
 
• **Bali:** A tribute paid by subjects to the king, often in the form of agricultural produce.
 
• **Bhaga:** A share of the agricultural produce collected as tax.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Gupta Administration:**

 
 
• The taxation system was structured to promote economic activities like agriculture and trade while ensuring adequate revenue for the state.
 
 
 
• **Gupta Economy:**
 
 
• The rulers encouraged the construction of irrigation systems and promoted agricultural activities, which formed the basis of their economy.
